regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the quality check is IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — both corroborate genuine investment-led expansion, not a statistical artefact. PMI Composite at 55.9 with services at 55.2 and manufacturing at 55.1 suggests the expansion is broad-based. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY, down from 5.0%, is the one dissenting voice — infrastructure-linked output is decelerating even as the investment cycle narrative strengthens.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY, up from 4.83% YoY in two months, is being driven by two distinct forces: food at 7.74% YoY (FAO food index at 136, rising) and fuel at 22.93% YoY — the highest in the dataset at the 95th percentile. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is the crucial counterpoint: it tells you the demand-side inflation is contained, but the RBI cannot cut into a 22.93% fuel print without risking a second-round wage-price spiral. The gap between headline and core is not comfort — it is a trap. If Brent holds at $109/bbl, the RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is already stale.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth of 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for two consecutive months — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 73rd percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-hold cycle, the eventual correction came through deposit rate wars that compressed NIMs before the regulator intervened with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending. NBFC credit accelerating to 15.8% YoY and services credit at 24.3% YoY are the pressure valves — if deposit mobilisation does not catch up within two quarters, the RBI's macro-prudential toolkit gets tested again.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with CPI at 5.54% YoY, the real repo rate is effectively negative 29 bps — accommodative by accident, not design. The RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is almost certainly being revised upward given fuel at 22.93% YoY. A rate cut in this environment is not a policy option; the question is whether the next move is a hike. For housing, a repo hold at 5.25% p.a. with average home loan rates already at 7.9% p.a. means affordability does not improve — and with INR at 95.24, imported inflation keeps the ceiling in place.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, up from 16.1% YoY, combined with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% and at the 74th percentile — is the most credible signal of a private capex upcycle in this dataset. The 77.4% threshold matters: historically, sustained utilisation above 75% is where private investment decisions get made, not announced. The inversion: credit to industry at 18.2% YoY is funding this capex, but if deposit growth does not support credit expansion, the funding cost for industrial borrowers rises — and capex IRRs that pencilled out at 5.25% p.a. Repo may not survive a 50 bps funding cost shock.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a 73rd-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the level: passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are falling for the second consecutive month (from 26.1% to 16.0% to 7.9%), while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounded sharply. This is the classic India dual-economy split — mass-market mobility (two-wheelers, rural demand) recovering while urban discretionary (passenger vehicles) decelerates. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is the tax on this consumption: every rupee spent at the pump is a rupee not spent at the mall, and e-commerce GMV at 12.4% YoY at the 15th percentile confirms the squeeze is already visible in digital spend.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"The deposit acceleration masks structural stress: banks are chasing credit growth via wholesale funding and NBFC partnerships. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and deposit franchises in metros; avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities. RBI will likely signal tighter liquidity ahead — position for 25-50 bps of rate cuts delayed into Q3 2026, not Q2. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month signals corporates are already hedging bank credit rationing.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile has preceded 2-3 quarters of NBFC stress and selective bank NPA spikes. Last time credit-deposit divergence was this wide (2022), RBI tightened liquidity and rates stayed elevated for 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Cyclicals","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest, up from 16.1% YoY), now at 52nd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 74th percentile — in the sweet spot for capex acceleration without overheating. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5%), but this masks divergence: credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (74th percentile), credit to services at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile, rising 2 months). Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile, rising 2 months) signals commercial vehicle and two-wheeler fleet expansion.","implication":"Capex is broadening from traditional infrastructure into services (GCCs, logistics, fintech) and commercial mobility. Overweight capital goods, auto ancillaries, and industrial equipment suppliers. Underweight pure-play infrastructure plays — they're already priced for capex. Expect 12-18 month tailwind for order books and working capital financing. RBI's rate pause is intentional: they're protecting capex momentum into FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 3 years and historically precedes 18-24 months of sustained capex. Last time CU was this high (2018), capex-to-GDP rose 200 bps over 2 years.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest), at 93rd percentile, rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (at 2nd percentile, data quality issue noted), but SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (89th percentile, up 2 of last 3 months). Average SIP AUM per account implies ticket size of ~₹17.7 lakh — up from ₹16.6 lakh 3 months ago. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile, up 2 of last 3 months). DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile).","implication":"SIP growth is decelerating in account count (10.7% YoY, at 30th percentile) but accelerating in AUM — affluent money is entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Rotate from small-cap/mid-cap to large-cap quality and dividend payers. FII outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) are offsetting DII strength — expect volatility if global liquidity tightens. Maintain overweight on Nifty 50 and Bank Nifty, but trim exposure to micro-cap and thematic funds.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile have historically preceded 6-12 month market consolidation, not acceleration. When SIP ticket size rises while account growth slows, retail is rotating to quality — a sign of maturation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY), at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at $109.37 / bbl (flat, 75th percentile); WTI at $98.41 / bbl (81st percentile). Natural gas at $3.035 / MMBtu (falling 5 in a row, 19th percentile) — no relief from energy costs. CPI headline at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83% YoY, rising 2 months), food inflation at 7.74% YoY (rising 2 months, 57th percentile). FAO food index at 136 (up 2 of last 3 months, 61st percentile).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the tail risk to RBI's inflation forecast (5.1% YoY). If Brent stays >$105 / bbl and geopolitical risk spikes, CPI could breach 6% by Q2 2026, forcing RBI to pause rate cuts indefinitely. Hedge via long crude positions or energy stocks; reduce exposure to rate-sensitive sectors (FMCG, auto). India's CAD will widen if oil stays elevated — watch INR weakness (currently at 95.24 ₹ / USD, 89th percentile). Import bill risk is material.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has preceded 2-3 quarters of RBI hawkishness and rate hikes. Last time fuel inflation spiked this high (2022), RBI kept rates elevated for 18 months despite growth slowdown.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Saturation","data_text":"Office absorption at 4 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, at 0th percentile — lowest in dataset), down from 21 mn sq ft / quarter 5 quarters ago. Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (up from 13.74%, 41st percentile). Nifty IT index flat YTD despite US PMI composite at 58.4 (91st percentile) and US GDP at 2.2% SAAR (rising 2 in a row). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹109 / sqft / month (61st percentile, up from ₹100.6), rent in Mumbai at ₹156 / sqft / month (59th percentile, up from ₹125) — rents rising but absorption collapsing. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (35th percentile, down from 11.6%) — retail is absorbing space faster than offices.","implication":"GCCs (Global Capability Centers) are consolidating, not expanding. The narrative of 'IT services growth = office demand' is broken. Capex in commercial real estate is shifting from office to logistics and retail. This explains why office REITs (Embassy at ₹369.92 / unit, down from ₹435.4; Mindspace at ₹345.06 / unit, down from ₹493.46) are underperforming despite strong GDP growth. Underweight office REITs; overweight logistics and retail REITs. IT services capex is moving to cloud and automation, not real estate. This is a 2-3 year structural headwind for Tier-1 office markets.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is a structural break. When office absorption collapses while GDP and PMI are strong, it signals a shift in how corporates deploy capital — away from real estate, toward technology and automation. This preceded the 2020-2021 office market downturn.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But Fuel Inflation Taxes the Consumer Silently

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY with PMI Composite at 55.9 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — investment-led expansion with broad sectoral confirmation.
  • But fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, highest in dataset) is compressing real household incomes — passenger vehicle sales have decelerated from 26.1% to 7.9% YoY over three months.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounded, signalling rural/mass-market resilience even as urban discretionary fades.
  • Core sector at 4.8% YoY, down from 5.0% — infrastructure output decelerating against the investment-cycle narrative.

The tension: Headline GDP and PMI signal expansion; the consumer-facing data — PV sales falling, e-commerce GMV at a 15th-percentile 12.4% YoY — signals a fuel-tax drag that the aggregates are not yet capturing.

Bottom line: Watch PV sales for a third consecutive monthly deceleration — if it prints below 5% YoY, the consumption leg of the growth story requires a downgrade.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Acceleration Meets Tightening Everywhere — EM Caught in the Middle

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile, rising two months) and US GDP at 2.2% SAAR (rising two months) — US growth is genuinely re-accelerating.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 5.09% yield (92nd percentile) and Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. (rising two months) mean the bond market is tightening for the Fed.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in dataset, rising two months) — yen carry unwind is structural, not episodic.
  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,145 (100th percentile) while Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY rising two months — European equities are pricing a soft landing the ECB's rate path does not support.

The tension: DM equity markets are at or near all-time highs while every major central bank is tightening or holding at cycle peaks — the divergence between asset prices and policy rates is the widest it has been this cycle.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underpriced tail risk for India: each 25 bps hike unwinds another layer of yen-funded EM carry, and FII equity net is already at -₹49,935 cr / month.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows Hold the Line — FII Exit Accelerates

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile, rising three consecutive months) — retail systematic flows are the market's shock absorber.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) absorbing FII equity net outflows of -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile).
  • But MF AUM fell to ₹82.64 lakh cr from ₹87.08 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion is shrinking the DII war chest even as flows hold.
  • NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) — institutional product launches have effectively stopped, signalling distributor caution.

The tension: SIP autopilot is keeping DII absorption intact, but falling MF AUM and near-zero NFO activity suggest the institutional infrastructure for sustained absorption is under quiet stress.

Bottom line: If SIP inflows break below ₹30,000 cr / month — the level where DII absorption no longer offsets FII outflows at current run-rates — Nifty support at 22,500 becomes the test.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty Prices the Lending Boom; REITs Price the Office Collapse

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 10 pp vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) sustaining purchasing power in MMR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and NCR.
  • Luxury (₹1.5–2.5 cr) and premium (₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr) together represent 55% of launch supply — NRI demand is structurally aligned with where developers are building.
  • Bank Nifty at 55,488 (91st percentile) while the CD ratio sits at 81% — the index is pricing credit growth, not the deposit funding gap beneath it.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down sharply from prior prints, consistent with office absorption at 4 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile).

The tension: Bank Nifty at a 91st-percentile high and REIT units at multi-quarter lows are two markets reading the same economy differently — one pricing the credit upcycle, the other pricing the GCC demand collapse.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 10 mn sq ft / quarter; hedge Bank Nifty longs against a macro-prudential risk-weight circular, which the CD ratio at 81% makes increasingly probable.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — The Fuel-FII-FX Triangle

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $109/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widening CAD ~40 bps and pressuring INR.
  • INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile, weakest in dataset) with FII equity outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month — gold in INR at an all-time high ₹12,712/g confirms the weakness is structural, not just USD strength.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — yen carry unwind has further to run; US 10Y at 5.09% yield keeps the pressure on EM allocations.
  • CD ratio at 81% with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if the gap widens another quarter, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights becomes the base case, not the tail.

The tension: The fuel-INR-FII loop is self-reinforcing: higher oil widens CAD, weakens INR, accelerates FII exit, weakens INR further — and the RBI cannot cut to defend growth without inflaming all three.

Bottom line: Watch Brent this week: a sustained print above $112/bbl breaks the RBI's 5.1% YoY inflation forecast and forces an explicit hawkish pivot, repricing the entire rate curve.

"}
